question.problem:
The parabola $y={x}^{2}+2x-3$ and the line $y=5x+7$ intersect at the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2}),$ where ${x}_{1}<{x}_{2}.$ Find the values of ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}.$

${y}_{1}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,{y}_{2}=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system consisting of the equations of the curves:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y={x}^{2}+2x-3 \\ y=5x+7\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x-3 & =5x+7 \\ {x}^{2}-3x-10 & =0 \\ (x+2)(x-5) & =0 \\ x & =-2,5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${x}_{1}<{x}_{2},$ the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points are ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=5.$

To find the $y$-coordinates of the intersection points, we plug these values into either curve. Let's choose the line since it's simpler.

- Substituting ${x}_{1}=-2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =5{x}_{1}+7 \\  & =5(-2)+7 \\  & =-3,\end{aligned}
$$

so one point of intersection is $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-2,-3).$

- Substituting ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{2} & =5{x}_{2}+7 \\  & =5(5)+7 \\  & =32,\end{aligned}
$$

so the other point of intersection is $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(5,32).$
